data.narrative:
Atom Bodies is a Series A biotech company founded by Tyler Hayes, Doug Satzger, and Eric Monsef, which has raised $142.2M to date. The valuation framework draws on a universe of 3 public comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private peers in the Biotech & Health sector, including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Given data constraints, only the stage-progression method is applicable. This approach uses the $142.2M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to derive an implied valuation of $284M. Peer-median triangulation was not executable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum dataset thresholds (fewer than three peers after filtering). Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples—the sector median stands at 7.4x across the three public tickers—cannot be applied without the target's disclosed revenue.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $242M to $327M, centered on $284M. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression point estimate. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue-based metrics, which prevents calibration against public multiples, and the thinness of same-stage private comparables. Validation would benefit from revenue disclosure or additional same-sector Series A reference points.
